import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/training_9.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and types
target_columns = ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']
target_dtypes = {
    'admit': 'int64',
    'gre': 'int64',
    'gpa': 'float64',
    'prestige': 'int64'
}

# Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)  # ignore the first numerical index column
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema
    df = df[target_columns]
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we can concatenate (union) all source tables vertically
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Enforce target data types explicitly
combined_df = combined_df.astype(target_dtypes)

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_7/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
